verdicts.reason: The cited workflow directly opens an issue detail URL, reads the body text, and derives open vs closed from the visible Open/Closed and Close issue/Reopen issue signals. The proposed method preserves that site-specific acquisition/parsing and returns a typed issue record without the workflow’s task-specific keyword search or boolean answer formatting.

The cited workflow opens each project page from START_URL plus href, reads body text, and parses visible Project ID and Star count with the same regexes. The method cleanly narrows that reusable site behavior into a typed project record and leaves zero-star filtering and cross-project aggregation to callers.

The cited workflow traverses dashboard issue list URLs, follows pagination via the next link, and extracts issue link text and hrefs matching /issues/{iid}. The method keeps that site-native listing behavior, returns typed issue summaries plus visited page URLs for completeness, and omits the workflow’s task-specific dependency keyword matching and cross-view decision logic.

The cited workflow navigates to /dashboard/projects, clicks the Personal filter, parses each project card from main .projects-list > li, and extracts the displayed path plus four visible counts. The method generalizes exactly that UI parsing into typed project summaries while excluding the workflow’s zero-star filtering and follow-up project-page inspection.

The cited workflow directly requests the project members page, extracts the data-members-data HTML attribute, unescapes and JSON-decodes it, and reads member objects from the embedded blob. The method retains that site-specific acquisition/parsing and returns typed member records and usernames without adding task-specific filtering or formatting.

The cited workflow calls the GitLab REST commits endpoint /api/v4/projects/{project_id}/repository/commits with since/until/per_page parameters and reads both the JSON payload and response headers. The method faithfully generalizes that site API access with authenticated cookies, typed commit objects, and pagination header signals while leaving author filtering and counting outside the primitive.

The cited workflow for task317_t324 supports navigating to the repository graphs branch page and parsing visible contributor names with commit counts from rendered page text. The method returns typed contributor records and explicitly marks the parse as incomplete rather than pretending to enumerate all contributors, so it avoids a completeness failure while keeping top-N/task-answer logic out of scope.
